summary: Former Tioga County lookout on Mount Tom; the register says a bald tower was used around 1917 and is no longer standing. Little else is documented.

events.note: Register says the bald tower was used circa 1917
Former Fire Lookout Sites Register entry dated September 16, 2008

evidence.supports: Bald tower used circa 1917 and no longer standing
evidence.quote: This bald tower was used circa 1917 and is no longer standing.

evidence.supports: Loop in Tioga State Forest near Wellsboro; climbs a steep ridge to a vista point near the summit
evidence.quote: The Mt Tom Loop at Tioga State Forest near Wellsboro, Pennsylvania is a strenuous 3.6-mile loop trail that leads straight up a steep ridge to a stunning vista point near the summit of Mount Tom.

evidence.supports: Trailhead at the main parking lot of the Darling Run Access Area, which serves the Pine Creek Trail
evidence.quote: The hike starts out at the main parking lot at the Darling Run Access Area for the Pine Creek Trail

evidence.supports: The one vista point on the route is well worth the climb
evidence.quote: The one vista point along this hike is well worth the work to get to the top.

notes_for_editor: The register page lists no coordinates ('No coordinates are available'), so the record's point 41.74507, -77.4072 has no register source; MyHikes lists the Mt. Tom Loop trailhead at 41.736337, -77.428898. Neither the register nor any page read says who built the tower, its height, when it came down, or what remains. Searches found only unrelated Mount Toms (Massachusetts, Connecticut, Indiana) and a geocache, none of them used. Access note is from a trail guide only; no source confirms the summit is open to visitors.
